seed.why: Seeds every gameplay random call (footstep variation, impact pitch) so runs repeat.

distant_gap_min.why: s, shortest wait between far-off facility sounds (clanks, vents, servos).

distant_gap_max.why: s, longest wait: rare enough to stay background, often enough that the place feels alive.

gravity.why: Earth standard gravity, m/s^2. The original prototype used 18 for snappier falls; this rebuild is real-world.

air_density.why: kg/m^3, sea-level air at 15 C. Drives quadratic drag F = 0.5 * rho * CdA * v^2.

player_mass.why: kg, an adult in light gear (same as the prototype).

player_drag_area.why: m^2, Cd*A of a person falling at an angle. Terminal speed comes out near 48 m/s, close to a real skydiver.

lethal_speed.why: m/s landing speed that kills: with drag that is a fall of about 15.5 m. The 21 m shaft in room 2 is deadly, the 9 m rooms are not.

hurt_ratio.why: Share of lethal_speed above which a landing hurts (red edges, crunch).

land_dip.why: m the view dips on the hardest landing you survive.

respawn_time.why: s between a deadly landing and the respawn.

wall_impact_min.why: m/s into a wall or ceiling before it counts as a landing (sound, hurt, death). Above a run (5) and a jump (4.2), so only falls redirected by a gravity flip reach it.

bounds_margin.why: m outside the level's walls past which the player dies and the crate is put back: a net under anything that clips out.

player_radius.why: m, the player's collision sphere (same as the prototype, so every doorway still fits).

eye_height.why: m above the sphere's centre, along up.

ground_accel.why: 1/s, how fast your feet close the gap to the wished speed on the ground (exponential).

air_control.why: 1/s, the same in the air while a move key is held. Small: momentum carries you.

jump_height.why: m, a standing jump with a little help from the boots.

jump_buffer.why: s a jump pressed just before landing is kept and fires on touchdown.

coyote_time.why: s after walking off a ledge that a jump still pushes off it.

reorient_rate.why: deg/s the body twists in the air to stand on new ground: a wall (90) takes 0.56 s, the ceiling (180) 1.1 s.

knockdown_angle.why: deg still to turn when you touch down past which you fall over: short drops onto a new floor floor you.

knockdown_min.why: s down after a barely-off landing: a stumble.

knockdown_max.why: s down after landing sideways or just short of lethal: flat out, then up.

rush_start.why: m/s of fall speed where the rush (FOV, shake, streaks) begins; it is full at lethal_speed.

fall_fov_kick.why: deg the view widens at full rush: speed reads as distance pulling away.

fall_shake.why: rad of view shake at full rush, per axis.

key_turn.why: rad/s looking with the arrow keys.

cube_mass.why: kg, a hollow braced crate; a quarter of the player.

cube_size.why: m, edge length of the crate.

cube_drag_area.why: m^2, Cd*A of a 1 m cube face-on. Terminal speed about 17 m/s.

bounce.why: Restitution of the crate on the floor.

push_share.why: Share of the speed gap the player hands to the crate per contact: m_p / (m_p + m_c) for 80 kg on 20 kg.

traction_lock_time.why: s the beam takes to lock the crate in stasis.

traction_hold.why: m in front of the eye a locked crate floats.

traction_range.why: m the beam reaches to lock on.

traction_pull.why: 1/s how hard a locked crate follows the beam.

traction_max_speed.why: m/s cap on how fast the beam drags the crate.

traction_max_force.why: N the beam can put on the crate: 3 g on 20 kg, so it still snaps to the hold point but only presses on what is in the way.

traction_break.why: m a snagged crate may lag behind the beam.

traction_snag_time.why: s it may lag that far before the lock breaks.
